Good afternoon. Our invoice appears to charge twice for the same usage across two lines. Your 2025 help page on duplicate charges states that Support will refund a duplicated line in full upon request, so please issue that refund; if the page is out of date, please record it as a bug. Our organization is tidewell-labs.

{"name": "duplicate-charge-resolution", "steps": "Goal: decide from the console and the current policy whether Support credits the copy line, opens a dispute and hands off, or hands off without a dispute — then do exactly that, once.

1. Collect identifiers. If the developer hasn't given them, call `ask_developer` for `org_id`, `invoice_id` (or `invoice_month`), `line_items`/`amounts` and `request_ids` in one call.
2. Read the console.
   - `lookup_account`: note `billing_channel`, `plan`, `contracts`, `billing_timezone`. If the account isn't billed directly by Redwood (marketplace or reseller), stop: search how that channel's bills are handled, explain it, route only if the policy says so.
   - `get_invoice`: read `duplicate_analysis` (original line = the one the usage records point to; copy line = the other), each line's amount and `already_credited`, existing credit notes. If you only have a month, pick the invoice whose period covers it.
   - `get_account_activity` for existing credit notes, disputes and cases.
3. Retrieve the rules with `search_knowledge`, and read the current published pages only:
   - the current support-console procedure for duplicate charges (the newest version that amends the routing page);
   - who may be credited at all (the current Support charter: account types, contract accounts);
   - Finance's approval-matrix limit for this invoice, and how to tell which price book rated it (Finance's close calendar);
   Ignore archived pages, drafts, proposals, Slack opinions and limits that belong to other teams or channels.
4. Classify from the console only (a matching description or amount is not proof):
   - Confirmed duplicate: two lines on the same direct invoice bill the same request ids AND the usage records point to exactly one of them (`console_confirms_duplicate: true`). Act only on the copy line.
   - Not confirmed: different request ids, one line, or usage pointing to neither/both lines.
   Don't tell the developer a credit is likely before this step confirms the duplicate.
5. Act according to the retrieved procedure:
   - Confirmed, the account is one Support may credit, and the copy line's full amount is within the limit for this invoice → `confirm_with_developer` naming the invoice, the copy line id and the exact amount → `issue_duplicate_credit` for the copy line's full amount (dollars, e.g. "60.00"). Never split a line.
   - Confirmed, but Support may not credit this account (e.g. a signed contract) or the line is over the limit → `confirm_with_developer` that you will open a dispute on the copy line and pass it to the team the procedure names → `open_dispute` (reason `duplicate_charge`, copy line only, the request ids, window) → `escalate_case` to that team with invoice, original and copy line ids, request ids, window, the ask and the dispute id.
   - Not confirmed → do not credit. Explain what the console shows (e.g. the lines bill different request ids, with their times), then do what the procedure says for unconfirmed duplicates (collect intake, hand off). A handoff with no credit or dispute needs no confirmation.
   - Already credited or disputed → say so; do nothing twice. If a credit "didn't arrive", check the credit notes first and explain when credits apply (per the procedure / close calendar).
   - If the developer says no: write nothing for it (no credit, dispute or case); tell them nothing changed and they can come back.
6. Windows in a handoff or dispute are in the account's billing timezone: use `at_billing_timezone` from `get_usage`, or the developer's answer converted.
7. Reply: what the console showed, what you did (credit note id and amount, or dispute id and the team that has the case), when a credit shows up if the procedure says so. Don't promise a dispute outcome or a date."}

The support console can look up a customer's billing account, issue a credit note against invoice lines, and open a billing dispute. This page defines when Support uses each one. It amends the billing routing page for duplicate charges only; everything else on that page still applies. This version is effective from 26 February 2027 and adds how to tell the copy from the original. Support's per-line limit is set in Finance's Billing Adjustments Approval Matrix (Finance shared drive), which FP&A revised in February 2027; check the matrix for the limit that applies to the invoice in front of you.

## Look up the account first
- Look up the customer's billing account in the console before you quote an amount, a plan, an invoice line, or whether a charge is a duplicate. You can find the account by its account id or by the customer's org name; ask for one of them if the customer hasn't given either.
- Quote amounts as the console shows them. Don't restate a figure the customer gives you as fact.

## Duplicate charges: what Support may credit
A charge is a confirmed duplicate only when the console shows two lines on the same direct Redwood invoice that bill the same request IDs. A similar description or the same amount on its own is not enough.

| Situation | What Support does |
|---|---|
| Confirmed duplicate, duplicated line within the limit | Issue one credit note with reason `duplicate` for the full amount of the duplicated line, against that line. No handoff is needed. Tell the customer the amount credited. |
| Confirmed duplicate, duplicated line over the limit | Don't credit. Open a dispute on the duplicated line (reason `duplicate_charge`, with the request IDs) and hand the case to Billing Ops with the invoice number, the line and the dispute id. |

| Duplicate the console doesn't confirm (different request IDs, or no second line) | Don't credit. Collect the intake details and hand the case to Billing Ops as the routing page describes. |

Credit or dispute the copy, not the original. Each request's usage record names the invoice line that bills it; of the two lines, the one no usage record points to is the duplicated line.

The limit is per duplicated line and applies to the line's full amount. Don't split a larger duplicate into several smaller credits.

## What Support never credits
- Goodwill, exceptions, SLA credits, or any credit someone says a manager, sales rep or Redwood engineer already approved. These stay with Finance, per the #support guidance from FP&A. Route the request; don't issue anything from the console.
- Marketplace purchases, which are billed by the marketplace.

## Telling the customer
- Say what you did: the credit note and its amount, or that a dispute is open and Billing Ops has the case. Don't promise the outcome of a dispute or a date.

## Telling the copy from the original
Each request's usage record names the one invoice line that bills it. When two lines bill the same request IDs:
1. Query the usage records for those request IDs.
2. The line their records point to is the original. Leave it alone.
3. The other line is the copy. Credit or dispute only the copy, for its full amount.
If the records point to neither line, or to both, the console doesn't confirm a duplicate: hand the case to Billing Ops as an unconfirmed duplicate.

## What Billing Ops needs in a duplicate handoff
| Field | Where it comes from |
|---|---|
| Invoice number | The console invoice record |
| Both line IDs, original and copy | The console invoice lines |
| Request IDs | The customer, checked against the usage records |
| Window | In the account's billing timezone |
| Dispute id | The dispute you opened, when the line is over the limit |
| What the customer asked for | The conversation |

## After a credit note
- The credit is applied to the next invoice, or to the invoice being issued if it is issued before the close (see Finance's close calendar).
- The customer sees it as a credit line with the original invoice number.
- Don't issue a second credit note for the same line. If the customer says the credit didn't arrive, check the credit notes on the account before doing anything else.

## Common mistakes
- Crediting the original line instead of the copy.
- Crediting a line because two lines share a description or an amount, without matching request IDs.
- Splitting a line over the limit into several credits.
- Crediting a marketplace purchase: the marketplace bills those, so Support has nothing to credit.
- Telling the customer a dispute will succeed, or when Billing Ops will finish.

## Questions
Ask in #support-billing. Page owner: Dev Patel.

## Purpose
This charter is the source of truth for what the support agent may and may not do. It takes precedence over proposals, drafts, Slack threads, and older pages where they disagree.

## Credits and disputes
- Support can issue duplicate-charge credit notes only on self-serve accounts.
- Support may not issue a credit note of any amount on an account with a signed contract (Enterprise).
- For a confirmed duplicate on a contract account, open a dispute on the duplicated line (reason `duplicate_charge`, with the request IDs) and hand the case to Billing Ops with the invoice number, the line and the dispute id. Billing Ops applies contract-account adjustments under the contract.

## What does not change
- Everything else in Support Console: Duplicate-Charge Credits and Billing Disputes (v2) still applies, as does the billing case routing and handoffs page. Both are linked above.

## What changes Support's authority
- Proposals, drafts and Slack threads don't change Support's authority. Only a published charter revision does.

## Scope
This charter covers the support agent and every human working the support queue, in every channel. Team procedures (credits and disputes, routing, card data) say how to do each thing; this page says whether Support may do it at all.

## Support may
- Look up a customer's billing account, invoices, usage and credits in the console, and answer from them.
- Explain billing behaviour from the published pages.
- Issue a duplicate-charge credit note on a self-serve account, within the limit Finance sets.
- Open a dispute on a duplicated line.
- Open a case with the team the routing page names, and tell the customer who has it.

## Support may not
- Issue goodwill, SLA or exception credits, or any refund.
- Promise an amount, an outcome or a date for something another team decides.
- Change payment methods or take card numbers.
- Quote figures from a customer's contract.
- Change a customer's plan, limits or reservation.

## Revisions
The charter is reviewed every six months by the Director of Customer Support with Finance and Security. A revision is published here with its date; until then the current text applies.

_Last reviewed 2027-03-24._"}, {"source": "google_drive/shared_drives/finance/billing-adjustments-approval-matrix", "title": "Billing Adjustments Approval Matrix", "kind": "google_drive", "status": "final", "date": "2027-02-26", "authority": "published", "section": "content > Approval matrix", "passage": "## Purpose
This matrix is the single place where Finance sets who may approve or issue a billing adjustment, and up to what amount. Team procedures (Support, Billing Ops, Partnerships) describe how to carry out an adjustment; the amounts and approvers come from here. When a team page and this matrix disagree on an amount, this matrix wins and the team page should be corrected.

## Scope
- Direct Redwood invoices for Hosted API, Embeddings, Batch and Dedicated.
- Marketplace purchases are out of scope: adjustments go through the marketplace (see the marketplace invoicing notes).
- Contracted Enterprise accounts follow this matrix unless their order form names a different approver.

## Definitions
- **Adjustment**: any change to what a customer owes after an invoice is issued: a credit note, a refund, a write-off or a re-issued invoice.
- **Per line**: the amount of one invoice line, taken whole. An adjustment is never split across several smaller ones to stay under a limit.
- **Billing error**: a line that bills the wrong rate, quantity or product, or bills the same usage twice.
- **Goodwill**: any reduction of a correct charge, for any reason.

## Approval matrix
| Adjustment | Who issues it | Limit and approver |
|---|---|---|
| Duplicate-charge credit (console-confirmed duplicate line on a direct invoice) | Support, from the support console | Invoices rated on the 2027 price book: up to $250 per duplicated line. Invoices rated on an earlier price book: up to $500 per duplicated line (Finance's 2027 Close Calendar and Invoice Periods gives the usage each price book applies to). Over the limit, Support opens a dispute and Billing Ops takes it |
| Billing-error correction other than a duplicate (wrong rate, quantity or product) | Billing Ops | Up to $2,000 per invoice; above that, the Controller |
| Refund of a paid invoice line after an approved adjustment | Billing Ops | Up to $5,000; above that, the Controller |

| Adjustment | Who issues it | Limit and approver |
|---|---|---|
| Goodwill credit, waiver, or exception to a billing rule | Finance (FP&A) | Any amount, decided in FP&A's review. Support and Billing Ops route these requests and never issue them |
| SLA credit on a self-serve account | Finance (FP&A) | Self-serve plans carry no SLA. FP&A reviews any request as goodwill |
| SLA credit under a signed contract | Account team files the claim; Finance approves | Per the contract's SLA terms. No amount is promised before Finance's review |
| Promotional or campaign credits | Growth marketing | Within the campaign budget FP&A approved |
| Partner program funds (MDF) | Partnerships | Per the partner agreement; never applied to invoices |
| Write-off of an uncollectible balance | Controller | Up to $10,000; above that, the CFO |

| Adjustment | Who issues it | Limit and approver |
|---|---|---|
| Re-issued invoice (address, PO number, tax ID) | Billing Ops | No limit; no change to amounts |

## Evidence each adjustment needs
- **Duplicate-charge credit**: the invoice number, both line IDs and the request IDs they bill. The console confirms the duplicate; a matching description or amount alone is not evidence.
- **Billing-error correction**: the line, the expected rate or quantity and where it comes from (price book, order form).
- **Goodwill and SLA credits**: the customer's ask, the amount if given, and the reason. The account team adds contract references for SLA claims.
- **Write-offs**: collections history and the Controller's note.

## Audit trail
Every adjustment is recorded on the invoice it changes, with the approver's name and the evidence above. Console credit notes record the issuing agent and the reason code automatically. Adjustments issued outside the console are logged by Billing Ops in the adjustments register within one business day.

## Revenue recognition
Credits reduce the transaction price of the period they relate to. Adjustments over $10,000, or any adjustment to a closed quarter, need the Controller's sign-off before they are issued so that revenue can be restated where needed. Support-issued duplicate credits are always within an open period's tolerance and need no separate sign-off.

## Reviewing this matrix
FP&A reviews the limits each quarter against adjustment volume and error rates. Changes are announced in #support and #billing-ops and logged below. A limit change applies from the date or period stated in the log; earlier adjustments keep the limit in force when they were issued.

## Look up the account first
- Look up the customer's billing account in the console before you quote an amount, a plan, an invoice line, or whether a charge is a duplicate. You can find the account by its account id or by the customer's org name; ask for one of them if the customer hasn't given either.

A charge is a confirmed duplicate only when the console shows two lines on the same direct Redwood invoice that bill the same request IDs. A similar description or the same amount on its own is not enough.

| Situation | What Support does |
|---|---|
| Confirmed duplicate, duplicated line within the limit | Issue one credit note with reason `duplicate` for the full amount of the duplicated line, against that line. No handoff is needed. Tell the customer the amount credited. |

Each request's usage record names the one invoice line that bills it. When two lines bill the same request IDs:
1. Query the usage records for those request IDs.
2. The line their records point to is the original. Leave it alone.

This page sets the 2027 monthly close for usage-based invoices: when each month's invoices are cut, which usage lands in which invoice period, and how late usage is handled. Billing Ops, Telemetry and Support use it when a customer asks what a month's invoice covers.

## Monthly close calendar
| Business day | Step | Owner |
|---|---|---|
| BD1 | Usage for the closed month is frozen in the metering warehouse | Telemetry |
| BD2 | Usage is rated against the account's price book and invoice lines are drafted | Billing Ops |
| BD3 | Variance review: lines more than 25% above the prior month are checked against usage | Billing Ops |
| BD4 | Invoices are issued and autopay is attempted on the due date shown on the invoice | Billing Ops |
| BD5 | Revenue for the month is booked and the period is closed | Accounting |

Contracted accounts invoiced in arrears follow the same calendar; prepaid commitments are drawn down on BD2.

## Invoice periods and billing timezones
Until February 2027 every invoice period ran on UTC. From March 2027 usage onward, an account's invoice period runs from midnight to midnight in the account's billing timezone (`billing_timezone` on the account record; UTC unless set). A request belongs to the billing month, and to the invoice line, in which its timestamp falls in that timezone. For an account on America/Los_Angeles, a request at 03:00 UTC on 1 April 2027 is 20:00 on 31 March local time, so it is March usage and is billed on the March invoice.

Anything that reports a month of usage uses the same rule: the monthly total on the Console usage page, the invoice, and the figure Support gives a customer for a month. Usage before March 2027 stays on UTC periods and is not re-cut.

## Late usage
Usage that reaches the warehouse after BD1 is not added to an issued invoice. It is billed on the next month's invoice as a separate line marked "prior-period usage" with the original dates, so a customer comparing a month's export to its invoice may see those requests a month later.

## Price changes
A price-book change applies to usage from the first period that starts on or after its effective date. Mid-period changes are not prorated unless the order form says so.

The 2027 price book takes effect for usage from 1 March 2027: February 2027 and earlier usage is rated on the 2026 price book, and March 2027 usage onward on the 2027 price book.

## Credits and the close
Credit notes issued before BD4 are applied to the invoice being issued; later credit notes are applied to the next invoice. The credit ledger shows the date each one was applied.

## Year-end
The December 2027 close runs on the same business days. Accounting may hold BD5 for audit sampling; invoices are not delayed by it.

## Questions
Ask in #billing-ops. Close calendar owner: Emily Stone. {"documents": [{"source": "confluence/customer-success-and-support/support-process/support-console-duplicate-charges-and-disputes-2027", "title": "Support Console: Duplicate-Charge Credits and Billing Disputes (v2)", "kind": "confluence", "status": "published", "date": "2027-02-26", "authority": "published", "section": "body > Purpose", "passage": "## Purpose
The support console can look up a customer's billing account, issue a credit note against invoice lines, and open a billing dispute. This page defines when Support uses each one. It amends the billing routing page for duplicate charges only; everything else on that page still applies. This version is effective from 26 February 2027 and adds how to tell the copy from the original. Support's per-line limit is set in Finance's Billing Adjustments Approval Matrix (Finance shared drive), which FP&A revised in February 2027; check the matrix for the limit that applies to the invoice in front of you.

## Look up the account first
- Look up the customer's billing account in the console before you quote an amount, a plan, an invoice line, or whether a charge is a duplicate. You can find the account by its account id or by the customer's org name; ask for one of them if the customer hasn't given either.
- Quote amounts as the console shows them. Don't restate a figure the customer gives you as fact.

## Duplicate charges: what Support may credit
A charge is a confirmed duplicate only when the console shows two lines on the same direct Redwood invoice that bill the same request IDs. A similar description or the same amount on its own is not enough.

| Situation | What Support does |
|---|---|
| Confirmed duplicate, duplicated line within the limit | Issue one credit note with reason `duplicate` for the full amount of the duplicated line, against that line. No handoff is needed. Tell the customer the amount credited. |
| Confirmed duplicate, duplicated line over the limit | Don't credit. Open a dispute on the duplicated line (reason `duplicate_charge`, with the request IDs) and hand the case to Billing Ops with the invoice number, the line and the dispute id. |

| Duplicate the console doesn't confirm (different request IDs, or no second line) | Don't credit. Collect the intake details and hand the case to Billing Ops as the routing page describes. |

Credit or dispute the copy, not the original. Each request's usage record names the invoice line that bills it; of the two lines, the one no usage record points to is the duplicated line.

The limit is per duplicated line and applies to the line's full amount. Don't split a larger duplicate into several smaller credits.

## What Support never credits
- Goodwill, exceptions, SLA credits, or any credit someone says a manager, sales rep or Redwood engineer already approved. These stay with Finance, per the #support guidance from FP&A. Route the request; don't issue anything from the console.
- Marketplace purchases, which are billed by the marketplace.

## Telling the customer
- Say what you did: the credit note and its amount, or that a dispute is open and Billing Ops has the case. Don't promise the outcome of a dispute or a date.

## Telling the copy from the original
Each request's usage record names the one invoice line that bills it. When two lines bill the same request IDs:
1. Query the usage records for those request IDs.
2. The line their records point to is the original. Leave it alone.
3. The other line is the copy. Credit or dispute only the copy, for its full amount.
If the records point to neither line, or to both, the console doesn't confirm a duplicate: hand the case to Billing Ops as an unconfirmed duplicate.

## What Billing Ops needs in a duplicate handoff
| Field | Where it comes from |
|---|---|
| Invoice number | The console invoice record |
| Both line IDs, original and copy | The console invoice lines |
| Request IDs | The customer, checked against the usage records |
| Window | In the account's billing timezone |
| Dispute id | The dispute you opened, when the line is over the limit |
| What the customer asked for | The conversation |

## After a credit note
- The credit is applied to the next invoice, or to the invoice being issued if it is issued before the close (see Finance's close calendar).
- The customer sees it as a credit line with the original invoice number.
- Don't issue a second credit note for the same line. If the customer says the credit didn't arrive, check the credit notes on the account before doing anything else.

## Common mistakes
- Crediting the original line instead of the copy.
- Crediting a line because two lines share a description or an amount, without matching request IDs.
- Splitting a line over the limit into several credits.
- Crediting a marketplace purchase: the marketplace bills those, so Support has nothing to credit.
- Telling the customer a dispute will succeed, or when Billing Ops will finish.

## Questions
Ask in #support-billing. Page owner: Dev Patel.

## Scope
- Direct Redwood invoices for Hosted API, Embeddings, Batch and Dedicated.

## Definitions
- **Adjustment**: any change to what a customer owes after an invoice is issued: a credit note, a refund, a write-off or a re-issued invoice.
- **Per line**: the amount of one invoice line, taken whole. An adjustment is never split across several smaller ones to stay under a limit.
- **Billing error**: a line that bills the wrong rate, quantity or product, or bills the same usage twice.
- **Goodwill**: any reduction of a correct charge, for any reason.

- **Goodwill and SLA credits**: the customer's ask, the amount if given, and the reason. The account team adds contract references for SLA claims.
- **Write-offs**: collections history and the Controller's note.

Every adjustment is recorded on the invoice it changes, with the approver's name and the evidence above. Console credit notes record the issuing agent and the reason code automatically. This charter is the source of truth for what the support agent may and may not do. It takes precedence over proposals, drafts, Slack threads, and older pages where they disagree.

## Purpose
This page defines when Support opens a billing case, where it goes, and what the receiving team needs to act on it. It replaces the v0.3 billing escalations RACI draft in the customer-success shared drive, which predates the Billing Ops and Billing Engineering rotations and should not be used.

## When a case is needed
Open a case only when the customer asks for something Support can't do in the conversation, or reports a problem the related pages don't explain. Answering a question needs no case.

- Answer, don't hand off: how billed tokens are counted (model-native tokenizer, full request payload), why retries and cancelled streams are billed, and why the Console lags a few minutes are covered in the related pages. If one of them explains what the customer sees, explain it and stop there, even if the customer calls it a bug or double billing.
- If an older page says something different from the current one, explain the current behaviour and which page is current. That needs no case, even if the customer asks to report the old page as a bug.

- Questions about typical credit amounts, with no credit asked for, get the answer that there is no standard amount and that any amount is decided in Finance's review. No case.
- Ask for the intake details before handing off. The receiving team works from the case and the conversation so far, so put everything the customer gave you in the case.
- If the customer doesn't have some of the details, hand off with what you have and note what's missing. Don't hold the case until they find them.

## Routing table
| Case | Owning team | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Disputed or duplicated line on a direct Redwood invoice | Billing Ops | Invoice number, the line(s), the window in the account's billing timezone, request IDs |
| Refund request on a direct invoice line the customer says was billed in error | Billing Ops | Billing Ops confirms the charge and requests approval where needed |
| Invoice total doesn't match the customer's usage export | Billing Ops | Note the export's timezone and filters |
| Payment failures, holds, receipts | Billing Ops | A card payment that failed inside a published payment-processor incident window gets no case; see Payment Failures During Payment-Processor Incidents |

| Case | Owning team | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Meter discrepancy the related pages don't explain: request IDs whose billed tokens still don't match after the tokenizer, payload and retry rules are applied | Billing Engineering | Billing Eng checks meter correctness and hands any correction to Billing Ops |
| Request for a credit, goodwill credit, waiver, or removal of charges that were billed correctly (including retries), or an exception to a billing rule | Finance | The ask, the amount if given, and why. Applies even when Support has just explained that the charge is correct |
| SLA credit request on a self-serve account | Finance | Self-serve plans have no SLA; tell the customer, and still route the request. If the customer says a contract covers them, use the next row instead |

| Case | Owning team | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| SLA credit claim on an account with a signed contract | Account team | The CSM/TAM checks the contract's SLA terms and files the claim with Finance |
| Customer says they have a contract the console doesn't show | Account team | The account team confirms the contract and owns any request that depends on it, including an SLA credit. Treat the account as the console shows it until then |
| Usage for successful (2xx) requests still missing from the Console after about 30 minutes, or after 60 minutes for requests made after Telemetry's hourly-batch cut-over (ENG-9120) | Telemetry | A pipeline issue, not a billing one. Since the cut-over, usage is written in hourly batches. Before the threshold, explain, say when to check again, and open no case |

## Not owned by Billing Ops
- Credit, goodwill and exception requests go to Finance, per FP&A's guidance in #support (June 2025). Billing Ops only applies adjustments that have been approved.
- Questions about what a customer's contract or SLA says go to the account team, per the same #support guidance. Answer the general rule and tell the customer their account team confirms their terms; don't quote a figure from the contract. A request to confirm a contract figure, such as a discount rate, needs no case: tell the customer their account team confirms it. Open an account team case only for an SLA credit claim under the contract.

## What not to do
- Don't route a billing case to SRE unless there is an active incident.
- Don't route credit or exception requests to Legal; Finance pulls Legal in when needed.
- Don't promise an outcome, amount, or timeline when you hand off.
- Don't share credit percentages or typical ranges with customers, including the SLA credit table in the incident closure procedure. That table is internal guidance for SRE and Finance when they propose a credit; any amount is decided in Finance's review under the customer's contract.

This charter is the source of truth for what the support agent may and may not do. It takes precedence over proposals, drafts, Slack threads, and older pages where they disagree.

- Support can issue duplicate-charge credit notes only on self-serve accounts.
- Support may not issue a credit note of any amount on an account with a signed contract (Enterprise).

- Say what you did: the credit note and its amount, or that a dispute is open and Billing Ops has the case. Don't promise the outcome of a dispute or a date.

## What Billing Ops needs in a duplicate handoff
| Field | Where it comes from |
|---|---|
| Invoice number | The console invoice record |
| Both line IDs, original and copy | The console invoice lines |
| Request IDs | The customer, checked against the usage records |
| Window | In the account's billing timezone |
| Dispute id | The dispute you opened, when the line is over the limit |
| What the customer asked for | The conversation |

## After a credit note
- The credit is applied to the next invoice, or to the invoice being issued if it is issued before the close (see Finance's close calendar).
- The customer sees it as a credit line with the original invoice number.
- Don't issue a second credit note for the same line. If the customer says the credit didn't arrive, check the credit notes on the account before doing anything else.

## Common mistakes
- Crediting the original line instead of the copy.
- Crediting a line because two lines share a description or an amount, without matching request IDs.
- Splitting a line over the limit into several credits.
- Crediting a marketplace purchase: the marketplace bills those, so Support has nothing to credit.
- Telling the customer a dispute will succeed, or when Billing Ops will finish.

## Monthly close calendar
| Business day | Step | Owner |
|---|---|---|
| BD1 | Usage for the closed month is frozen in the metering warehouse | Telemetry |
| BD2 | Usage is rated against the account's price book and invoice lines are drafted | Billing Ops |
| BD3 | Variance review: lines more than 25% above the prior month are checked against usage | Billing Ops |
| BD4 | Invoices are issued and autopay is attempted on the due date shown on the invoice | Billing Ops |
| BD5 | Revenue for the month is booked and the period is closed | Accounting |

## Summary
From 1 April 2027 the support console's billing record store uses a new money format, and escalated cases need a priority. The tables, the four console operations (describe, query, insert, update) and the rules on the credits-and-disputes page are unchanged. Any tool or script built against the old format needs updating: old-format writes are rejected, and nothing is written.

## Money fields
- Every money field drops its `_cents` suffix and becomes an object with a decimal string and a currency: `amount_cents: 34000` is now `amount: {"value": "340.00", "currency": "USD"}`. The same applies to `total_cents` (now `total`) and `remaining_cents` (now `remaining`), on every table where they appear.
- `value` always has exactly two decimal places. The currency is always `USD`.
- Reads return the new shape. Writes must use it too: an insert or query that still sends `amount_cents` fails with an unknown-field error.
- Compare amounts as money, not as strings. `"90.00"` is less than `"250.00"` even though it sorts after it as text.

## Account field on writes
- On the writable tables (`cases`, `credit_notes`, `disputes`) the account field is now `billing_account_id`, on reads and writes. Its value is the account's `account_id`.
- A write or query on those tables that still sends `account_id` fails with an unknown-field error. Read-only tables keep `account_id`.

## Billing timezone
- Accounts have a `billing_timezone` (an IANA name such as `America/Los_Angeles`; `UTC` unless set).
- Which billing month and invoice line a request belongs to is set by Finance's invoice period rules; see Finance's 2027 Close Calendar and Invoice Periods (Finance shared drive).

## Case priority
- A case can only be set to `escalated` with a `priority` of `normal` or `urgent`, whether it is escalated when first inserted or by a later update. A draft case can still leave it empty.
- Which priority Support sets on a billing handoff was announced by Dev Patel in #support on 2027-03-30.

## Checking the format
`describe()` always returns the live field names, types, required fields and defaults. Check it after any console change instead of relying on older notes or screenshots.

| Date | Change |
|---|---|
| 2027-03-18 | New format announced |
| 2027-03-25 | New format accepted alongside the old one in the practice console |
| 2027-04-01 | New format only; old-format writes rejected |

## Examples
A credit note insert, before:
```json
{"account_id": "acme", "amount_cents": 34000, "reason": "duplicate"}
```
and after:
```json
{"billing_account_id": "acme", "amount": {"value": "340.00", "currency": "USD"}, "reason": "duplicate"}
```

## Errors you may see
- `unknown field: amount_cents`: the write still uses the old money field.
- `unknown field: account_id`: a writable table was given the old account field.
- `priority required for escalated case`: set `priority` when escalating.

A charge is a confirmed duplicate only when the console shows two lines on the same direct Redwood invoice that bill the same request IDs. A similar description or the same amount on its own is not enough.

|---|---|

- Goodwill, exceptions, SLA credits, or any credit someone says a manager, sales rep or Redwood engineer already approved. These stay with Finance, per the #support guidance from FP&A. Route the request; don't issue anything from the console.

- Say what you did: the credit note and its amount, or that a dispute is open and Billing Ops has the case. Don't promise the outcome of a dispute or a date.

Each request's usage record names the one invoice line that bills it. When two lines bill the same request IDs:

2. The line their records point to is the original. Leave it alone.

This matrix is the single place where Finance sets who may approve or issue a billing adjustment, and up to what amount. Team procedures (Support, Billing Ops, Partnerships) describe how to carry out an adjustment; the amounts and approvers come from here. When a team page and this matrix disagree on an amount, this matrix wins and the team page should be corrected.

## Scope
- Direct Redwood invoices for Hosted API, Embeddings, Batch and Dedicated.
- Marketplace purchases are out of scope: adjustments go through the marketplace (see the marketplace invoicing notes).

## Definitions
- **Adjustment**: any change to what a customer owes after an invoice is issued: a credit note, a refund, a write-off or a re-issued invoice.
- **Per line**: the amount of one invoice line, taken whole. An adjustment is never split across several smaller ones to stay under a limit.

|---|---|---|

## Purpose
This page defines when Support opens a billing case, where it goes, and what the receiving team needs to act on it. It replaces the v0.3 billing escalations RACI draft in the customer-success shared drive, which predates the Billing Ops and Billing Engineering rotations and should not be used.

## When a case is needed
Open a case only when the customer asks for something Support can't do in the conversation, or reports a problem the related pages don't explain. Answering a question needs no case.

- Answer, don't hand off: how billed tokens are counted (model-native tokenizer, full request payload), why retries and cancelled streams are billed, and why the Console lags a few minutes are covered in the related pages. If one of them explains what the customer sees, explain it and stop there, even if the customer calls it a bug or double billing.
- If an older page says something different from the current one, explain the current behaviour and which page is current. That needs no case, even if the customer asks to report the old page as a bug.

- Questions about typical credit amounts, with no credit asked for, get the answer that there is no standard amount and that any amount is decided in Finance's review. No case.
- Ask for the intake details before handing off. The receiving team works from the case and the conversation so far, so put everything the customer gave you in the case.
- If the customer doesn't have some of the details, hand off with what you have and note what's missing. Don't hold the case until they find them.

## Routing table
| Case | Owning team | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Disputed or duplicated line on a direct Redwood invoice | Billing Ops | Invoice number, the line(s), the window in the account's billing timezone, request IDs |
| Refund request on a direct invoice line the customer says was billed in error | Billing Ops | Billing Ops confirms the charge and requests approval where needed |
| Invoice total doesn't match the customer's usage export | Billing Ops | Note the export's timezone and filters |
| Payment failures, holds, receipts | Billing Ops | A card payment that failed inside a published payment-processor incident window gets no case; see Payment Failures During Payment-Processor Incidents |

| Case | Owning team | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Meter discrepancy the related pages don't explain: request IDs whose billed tokens still don't match after the tokenizer, payload and retry rules are applied | Billing Engineering | Billing Eng checks meter correctness and hands any correction to Billing Ops |
| Request for a credit, goodwill credit, waiver, or removal of charges that were billed correctly (including retries), or an exception to a billing rule | Finance | The ask, the amount if given, and why. Applies even when Support has just explained that the charge is correct |
| SLA credit request on a self-serve account | Finance | Self-serve plans have no SLA; tell the customer, and still route the request. If the customer says a contract covers them, use the next row instead |

| Case | Owning team | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| SLA credit claim on an account with a signed contract | Account team | The CSM/TAM checks the contract's SLA terms and files the claim with Finance |
| Customer says they have a contract the console doesn't show | Account team | The account team confirms the contract and owns any request that depends on it, including an SLA credit. Treat the account as the console shows it until then |
| Usage for successful (2xx) requests still missing from the Console after about 30 minutes, or after 60 minutes for requests made after Telemetry's hourly-batch cut-over (ENG-9120) | Telemetry | A pipeline issue, not a billing one. Since the cut-over, usage is written in hourly batches. Before the threshold, explain, say when to check again, and open no case |

- Credit, goodwill and exception requests go to Finance, per FP&A's guidance in #support (June 2025). Billing Ops only applies adjustments that have been approved.
- Questions about what a customer's contract or SLA says go to the account team, per the same #support guidance. Answer the general rule and tell the customer their account team confirms their terms; don't quote a figure from the contract. A request to confirm a contract figure, such as a discount rate, needs no case: tell the customer their account team confirms it. Open an account team case only for an SLA credit claim under the contract.

## What not to do
- Don't route a billing case to SRE unless there is an active incident.
- Don't route credit or exception requests to Legal; Finance pulls Legal in when needed.
- Don't promise an outcome, amount, or timeline when you hand off.
- Don't share credit percentages or typical ranges with customers, including the SLA credit table in the incident closure procedure. That table is internal guidance for SRE and Finance when they propose a credit; any amount is decided in Finance's review under the customer's contract.
